title: Grant overruns a Confederate camp at Belmont, Missouri
description: Union troops under Brigadier General Ulysses S. Grant overran a Confederate camp at Belmont, Missouri, but were forced to retreat when Confederate reinforcements arrived. It was Grant's first combat test of the war, against Major General Leonidas Polk.

title: Black and white workers begin a general strike in New Orleans
description: A general strike began in New Orleans, Louisiana, and despite appeals to racial hatred its black and white trade unionists remained united. It ended on 12 November with the unions gaining most of their original demands.

title: More than 50 people are executed in the Stockholm Bloodbath
description: After Christian II was crowned king of Sweden, Archbishop Gustav Trolle questioned at Tre Kronor castle whether the former regent Sten Sture the Younger and his supporters were guilty of heresy. The trial ended in the execution of more than 50 people.

title: Shivaji kills Afzal Khan and routs the Bijapur army at Pratapgad
description: Shivaji killed the Bijapur general Afzal Khan, and his Maratha forces defeated the Bijapur troops at Pratapgad, the Marathas' first significant military triumph against a major regional power. Shivaji captured 65 elephants, 4,000 horses and 1,200 camels.

title: White supremacists overthrow the elected government of Wilmington
description: White supremacists in Wilmington, North Carolina, massacred black residents and overthrew the city's elected government, the only such coup against a municipal government in United States history. Studies since 2016 have called it terrorism.

title: The Council of Constance elects Martin V, ending the Western Schism
description: The Council of Constance elected Oddone Colonna as Pope Martin V, having deposed or accepted the resignation of the remaining papal claimants. His election ended the Western Schism of 1378, in which bishops in Rome and Avignon had both claimed to be pope.

title: Riots break out in Lhasa after the murder of Tibet's expected regent
description: An uprising began in Lhasa after two Qing ambans assassinated Gyurme Namgyal, the expected new regent of Tibet; both ambans were killed, with 51 Qing soldiers and 77 Chinese citizens. A year later the Qing executed the rebel leader Lobsang Trashi.

skip: a single shipwreck (SS Vestris): trivial for the site, and the lead gives no wider consequence

title: Breckinridge's Confederates rout Union troops at Bull's Gap
description: The three-day Battle of Bull's Gap in Hamblen and Greene counties, Tennessee, ended in a Union rout, as Confederates under Major General John C. Breckinridge pursued them to Strawberry Plains. Breckinridge had been vice president from 1857 to 1861.

skip: a single lifeboat disaster: trivial for the site, and the lead cannot carry two sentences

title: Police raid a summit of the American Mafia at Apalachin, New York
description: Law enforcement raided a national Mafia summit at Joseph Barbara's home in Apalachin, New York, and many Mafia figures were arrested trying to flee. Vito Genovese had wanted it to legitimize his new power; an estimated 100 Mafiosi are thought to have attended.

title: Ruby Bridges enters an all-white school in New Orleans
description: Ruby Bridges became the first African American child to attend the formerly whites-only William Frantz Elementary School in Louisiana, during the New Orleans school desegregation crisis. Norman Rockwell painted her in The Problem We All Live With (1964).

title: Enslaved people break out in revolt in the Cherokee Nation
description: A group of 20 African Americans enslaved by the Cherokee escaped in Indian Territory and set out for Mexico, where slavery had been abolished in 1829. Joined by 15 more from the Creek Nation, it was the largest such escape in the Cherokee Nation.
source: 1842 Slave Revolt in the Cherokee Nation

skip: a single steamboat explosion: trivial for the site (the main article is a one-line definition of a boiler explosion)

title: The Taira defeat Minamoto no Yoshinaka's fleet off Mizushima
description: In the Genpei War, an army sent by Minamoto no Yoshinaka across the Inland Sea against the Taira base at Yashima was caught by the Taira off Mizushima in Bitchu Province. The Taira tied their ships together with planks across them and defeated it.

title: The Montreal and Lachine Railroad opens, Montreal's first railway
description: Montreal's first railroad opened, running 12 km from Bonaventure Station in Montreal to the St. Lawrence River at Lachine to bypass the Lachine Rapids. Through later mergers it was eventually absorbed by the Grand Trunk Railway.

title: TVB begins broadcasting as Hong Kong's first wireless commercial station
description: TVB began broadcasting in Hong Kong, the first wireless commercial television station there. It became a cultural powerhouse in the Chinese-speaking world, known for its television dramas and for launching the careers of many Hong Kong actors and artists.

title: The Peace of Cremona ends a war between Venice and Milan
description: The Republic of Venice and the Duchy of Milan made the Peace of Cremona, ending the fourth of five campaigns in their long conflict for mastery in northern Italy. In the war Venice had hauled a fleet overland to Lake Garda, the Galeas per montes.

title: Rival factions in Rome elect Symmachus and Laurentius as pope
description: After the death of Anastasius II, Symmachus was elected pope in the Lateran Palace, while a faction with Byzantine sympathies elected Laurentius at Santa Maria Maggiore. The schism split the church, the Senate and the people of Rome.

title: The Congress of Manastir standardizes the Albanian alphabet
description: A national conference held in Manastir from 14 November closed, having set out to standardize the Albanian alphabet, until then written in six or more distinct alphabets. The day is kept as Alphabet Day in Albania, Kosovo and North Macedonia.

title: Enslaved Akwamu people rise against the planters of St. John
description: 150 enslaved people from Akwamu, in present-day Ghana, revolted against the owners and managers of the plantations on Sankt Jan (St. John) in the Danish West Indies. The colony's other islands were Saint Thomas and Saint Croix.

title: Assassins kill High Duke Leszek the White at Gąsawa
description: At a council of Polish Piast dukes near Gąsawa in Kuyavia, attackers assassinated Leszek the White, High Duke of Poland, and gravely wounded Duke Henry the Bearded of Silesia. Henry survived to become High Duke of all Poland from 1232.

title: South Carolina passes the Ordinance of Nullification
description: A South Carolina state convention declared the federal Tariffs of 1828 and 1832 null and void within the state, beginning the nullification crisis. Andrew Jackson threatened to send troops; after Congress lowered the tariff, the state repealed the ordinance.

title: A tsunami wrecks ships at Naples and ports along the Amalfi Coast
description: An earthquake shook Naples, and a tsunami in the Tyrrhenian Sea destroyed many ships there and many ports along the Amalfi Coast, Amalfi among them. Petrarch, whose ship was forced back to port, recorded it in his Epistolae familiares.

title: A great earthquake and tsunami strike the coast of Sumatra
description: An earthquake with an estimated magnitude of 8.8–9.2 struck Sumatra at about 22:00 local time, and a large tsunami flooded the island's southwestern coast. No reliable record of the dead survives; its size was later estimated from uplift in coral microatolls.

title: The Song fleet defeats Jin ships at Caishi on the Yangtze
description: A Song dynasty fleet fought Jin dynasty ships at Caishi on the Yangtze river, a major naval engagement of the Jin–Song Wars. The two-day battle ended in a decisive Song victory, aided by the Song's use of gunpowder weapons.

title: An earthquake devastates Fes and Meknes in Morocco
description: An earthquake of estimated magnitude 6.5 to 7.0 devastated the cities of Fes and Meknes in Morocco, killing at least 15,000 people in both cities. It struck less than a month after the earthquake of 1 November that had devastated Morocco and Lisbon.

skip: the founding of a professional society (the American Statistical Association): trivial for the site

title: New Zealand goes to the polls as the first nation where all women may vote
description: New Zealand's European electorates voted in a general election after campaigners led by Kate Sheppard had made it the first nation where all women had the right to vote in parliamentary elections. The Liberal Party won; Richard Seddon became prime minister.

title: The Abbasids defeat the Qarmatians at the Battle of Hama
description: An Abbasid army under Muhammad ibn Sulayman al-Katib defeated pro-Isma'ili Bedouin near Hama in Syria, capturing and executing their leaders. The victory paved the way for the Abbasid reconquest of the Tulunid domains in southern Syria and Egypt.

skip: a magnitude 5.3 earthquake in New Jersey: trivial for the site

title: Hood's Army of Tennessee suffers heavy losses at Franklin
description: John Bell Hood's Confederate Army of Tennessee made repeated frontal assaults on Union forces under John Schofield at Franklin, Tennessee, but could not stop their planned withdrawal to Nashville. It was one of the worst Confederate disasters of the war.

title: Tuscany becomes the first modern state to abolish the death penalty
description: Grand Duke Pietro Leopoldo, Leopold I of Tuscany, who opposed capital punishment and torture, abolished both in the Grand Duchy of Tuscany, the first state in modern history to do so. The day is kept as the Feast of Tuscany and as Cities for Life Day.

title: Lincoln's second State of the Union presses for ending slavery
description: In his second State of the Union Address to the 37th Congress, Abraham Lincoln reaffirmed the necessity of ending slavery. His Emancipation Proclamation of a month later made more than 3.5 million people enslaved in the Confederate states legally free.

title: Shaw University is founded in Raleigh, North Carolina
description: Shaw University began as a theological class of freedmen in the Guion Hotel in Raleigh, North Carolina; it is the oldest historically Black university to begin offering courses in the South. It took its name from Elijah Shaw in 1870.

title: Leipzig University is founded by the rulers of Saxony and Meissen
description: Frederick I, Elector of Saxony, and his brother William II, Margrave of Meissen, founded the university of Leipzig with the four scholastic faculties. Germany's second-oldest university, it has taught for over 600 years without interruption.

title: Colonial forces and gold miners fight at the Eureka Stockade
description: Gold miners and colonial forces fought at the Eureka Stockade in Ballarat, Victoria, the culmination of the 1851–1854 Eureka Rebellion; at least 27 died, most of them rebels. The miners' chief grievance was the cost of mining permits.

title: Sztáray's Austrians defeat the French at Wiesloch
description: Lieutenant Field Marshal Anton Sztáray, commanding the far right wing of the Austrian army in Swabia, defeated the French at Wiesloch in the War of the Second Coalition. The victory drove the French from the right bank of the Rhine and relieved Philippsburg.

title: Fifty Christians are burned alive in the Great Martyrdom of Edo
description: In Edo, the city now called Tokyo, 50 foreign and domestic Catholics, known as kirishitans, were burned alive for their Christianity. The executions are remembered as the Great Martyrdom of Edo.

title: Charles XI defeats the invading Danish army at the Battle of Lund
description: A Swedish army of about 8,000 under Charles XI defeated a Danish army of some 13,000 under Christian V north of Lund in Scania, in the Scanian War. By casualty percentage it is one of the bloodiest battles ever fought in Scandinavia.

title: Italy's largest recorded earthquake strikes the Kingdom of Naples
description: An earthquake of estimated magnitude 7.19–7.4, centred near Pontelandolfo, caused widespread destruction across central and southern Italy, with up to 70,000 deaths reported. With the shocks of 30 December it is the largest sequence in Italian history.

title: Georgia ratifies the Thirteenth Amendment, abolishing slavery
description: Georgia ratified the Thirteenth Amendment to the United States Constitution, which made slavery illegal except as punishment for a crime; that day it reached the required 27 of the then 36 states. It was the first of the three Reconstruction Amendments.

title: Venus crosses the Sun in the last transit of the 19th century
description: The transit of Venus, the second and last of the 19th century after that of 1874, was watched by many expeditions sent out by the European powers. The United States Congress alone sent eight to describe the two transits.

title: Mackenzie's rebels are crushed at Montgomery's Tavern near Toronto
description: British authorities and Canadian volunteers crushed the insurrection inspired by William Lyon Mackenzie near John Montgomery's tavern on Yonge Street, north of Toronto. It was the only battle of the Upper Canada Rebellion.

title: Chile's government defeats liberal rebels at Loncomilla
description: Conservative government forces defeated the liberal rebel army of José María de la Cruz, aided by the Mapuche chief Mañil and his warriors, at Loncomilla. The victory crushed the 1851 Chilean Revolution against President Manuel Montt.

title: A woman plays Desdemona on the English public stage for the first time
description: A woman, either Margaret Hughes or Anne Marshall, appeared on an English public stage for the first time, as Desdemona in Shakespeare's Othello. Hughes is often credited as the first professional actress on the English stage.

title: Congress sets up the Joint Committee on the Conduct of the War
description: The United States Congress set up the Joint Committee on the Conduct of the War to investigate the progress of the Civil War against the Confederacy. Meeting in secret but issuing reports from time to time, it was dismissed in May 1865.

title: P. B. S. Pinchback becomes acting governor of Louisiana
description: Pinckney Benton Stewart Pinchback, a Republican, became governor of Louisiana after Henry C. Warmoth's impeachment and served for 35 days. He is commonly called the first African American governor, though Dunn had served as acting governor in 1871.

title: Birger's brothers are seized at the Nyköping Banquet
description: At King Birger of Sweden's Christmas celebration at Nyköping Castle, his brothers Duke Valdemar and Duke Eric were imprisoned that night; they are assumed to have starved to death in its dungeon. The chief source is the very biased Eric Chronicle.

title: Indiana is admitted to the Union as the 19th state
description: Indiana, lying between Lake Michigan to the northwest and the Ohio River to the south, was admitted to the Union as the 19th state of the United States. Nicknamed the Hoosier State, it has Indianapolis as its capital and largest city.

title: Japanese aircraft bomb and sink the US gunboat Panay
description: Japanese aircraft attacked the U.S. Navy gunboat Panay and three Standard Oil tankers on the Yangtze near Nanjing, sinking the Panay, though Japan and the United States were not at war. It served on the Yangtze Patrol, begun after the Second Opium War.

title: Union troops under Hazen seize Fort McAllister near Savannah
description: Union forces under William B. Hazen overwhelmed the small Confederate force holding Fort McAllister, on the Ogeechee River near Savannah, Georgia, late in Sherman's March to the Sea. Its fall allowed Sherman to capture Savannah.

title: The Duke William sinks carrying deported Acadians to France
description: The ship Duke William, carrying Acadians deported from Île Saint-Jean to France in the Seven Years' War, sank in the North Atlantic with the loss of over 360 lives. It was one of the worst marine disasters in Canadian history.

title: John VIII becomes pope on the death of Adrian II
description: John VIII became bishop of Rome and leader of the Papal States on the day his predecessor, Pope Adrian II, died. He is often considered one of the most able popes of the 9th century.

title: St. Lucia's flood drowns tens of thousands in the Low Countries
description: A storm tide on St. Lucia Day and the day after drove the North Sea over seawalls and dykes, flooding much of the Low Countries and killing approximately 50,000 to 80,000 people. It was one of the largest floods in recorded history.

title: Sergius I is elected pope as a compromise between two rivals
description: Sergius I was elected bishop of Rome while two rivals, Paschal and Theodore, were disputing which of them should become pope. His refusal to accept the canons of the Quinisext Council later led Emperor Justinian II to order his arrest.

title: Stephen the Great defeats Matthias Corvinus at the Battle of Baia
description: Stephen the Great, prince of Moldavia, defeated the Hungarian king Matthias Corvinus, who was wounded three times, at Baia. Matthias had invaded Moldavia after Stephen annexed Chilia, a Black Sea fortress and harbour, from Hungarian and Wallachian forces.

title: A great earthquake strikes Valdivia in Chile
description: An earthquake of estimated magnitude 8.5 on the surface-wave scale, and 9.0 or more on the moment magnitude scale, struck Valdivia, Chile, at 14:30 local time. It led to the flood of Valdivia.

title: Mount Fuji begins its last confirmed eruption
description: The Hōei eruption of Mount Fuji began under the shogun Tokugawa Tsunayoshi and lasted until 24 February 1708, its last confirmed eruption. Its immense ash-fall over eastern Japan was followed by landslides and starvation across the country.

title: The Aztec sun stone is rediscovered in Mexico City's Zócalo
description: During repairs on Mexico City Cathedral, the Aztec sun stone, a Mexica sculpture 3.6 metres across buried in the Zócalo after the Spanish conquest, was rediscovered. It was mounted on an outer wall of the cathedral, where it stayed until 1885.

title: An earthquake and tsunami strike Keelung and Taipei in Taiwan
description: A magnitude 7.0 earthquake off northern Taiwan seriously damaged Keelung and Taipei, and its tsunami drowned hundreds; the death toll was estimated at 580. It is possibly the only confirmed widely destructive and deadly tsunami in Taiwan's history.

title: Cromwell's Whitehall Conference on readmitting Jews ends
description: A conference of English merchants, clergymen and lawyers called by Oliver Cromwell ended its debate on readmitting Jews to England, finding no law that prevented their return. Edward I's Edict of Expulsion had banned them in 1290.

title: Paolo Scolari is elected pope as Clement III
description: Paolo Scolari was elected pope as Clement III. He ended the conflict between the papacy and the city of Rome by allowing the election of magistrates, which brought the papacy back to the city after a six-year exile.

title: Thomas Paine publishes the first pamphlet of The American Crisis
description: The first pamphlet of Thomas Paine's series The American Crisis appeared in The Pennsylvania Journal, signed "Common Sense". The series ran to thirteen numbered pamphlets by 1777 and three more by 1783, during the American Revolution.

title: The Soviet government founds the Cheka, its first secret police
description: The Council of People's Commissars of the Russian SFSR set up the All-Russian Extraordinary Commission, the Cheka, the first Soviet secret police, under Felix Dzerzhinsky. By the end of the Russian Civil War in 1922 it had at least 200,000 personnel.

title: Honorius II is consecrated pope after Celestine II steps aside
description: Lamberto Scannabecchi became pope as Honorius II. Teobaldo Boccapecci, elected as Celestine II after the death of Callixtus II, had resigned before his consecration when factional violence broke out at his investiture.

title: An earthquake damages the missions of Santa Barbara and Ventura
description: An earthquake in present-day southern California severely damaged buildings and Spanish missions around Santa Barbara and Ventura. Only one person was killed, as a foreshock 15 minutes earlier had sent residents fleeing their buildings.

title: Yohl Ikʼnal takes the throne of the Maya city of Palenque
description: Yohl Ikʼnal, also known as Lady Kan Ik and Lady Kʼanal Ikʼnal, acceded to the throne of the Maya city-state of Palenque as queen regnant. She ruled Palenque until her death in 604.

title: Moscow's ballet school, later the Bolshoi Ballet Academy, is founded
description: The Moscow State Academy of Choreography, now the school of the Bolshoi Ballet, was founded under Catherine II as the second ballet school in Russia. It engaged the Italian teacher-choreographer Filippo Becari to teach children to dance.

title: John IV is elected pope after a four-month vacancy
description: John IV became bishop of Rome after a four-month vacancy. He wrote to the clergy of Ireland and Scotland about their mistakes in the time of keeping Easter, and he condemned Monothelitism as heresy.

title: The Marathas defeat the Nizam and Mughal generals at Bhopal
description: The Maratha Empire defeated the combined army of the Nizam of Hyderabad and several Mughal generals at Bhopal, a coalition that also took in the Rajputs of Jaipur and the Nawabs of Awadh and Bengal. The first Nizam had set up his own realm in 1724.

title: Aurelian dedicates a temple to Sol Invictus in Rome
description: The emperor Aurelian dedicated the Temple of the Sun in Rome to Sol Invictus, fulfilling a vow made after his campaign against Palmyra and paid for with its spoils. He promoted Sol Invictus as the chief god of the empire.

title: The Bishop of Utrecht's army attacks Utrecht men at Westbroek
description: An army of 4,000 to 5,000 raised by David of Burgundy, Bishop of Utrecht, attacked an armed band from Utrecht seeking to avenge the massacre of the people of Westbroek. It was one of the last battles of the Hook and Cod wars.

title: A fire at the Richmond Theatre kills Virginia's governor
description: A fire destroyed the Richmond Theatre in Richmond, Virginia, killing 72 people, among them Governor George William Smith and former senator Abraham B. Venable. It was the worst urban disaster in U.S. history at the time.

title: Spain issues the Laws of Burgos for its settlers in the Americas
description: Promulgated at Burgos after friars and academics pressed Ferdinand II and Joanna of Castile, the Laws of Burgos were the first codified laws on the conduct of Spaniards toward the Indigenous peoples of the Americas. They forbade their enslavement.

title: Tagore's "Jana Gana Mana" is first sung in public in Calcutta
description: Rabindranath Tagore's Bengali song "Bharoto Bhagyo Bidhata" was first sung publicly at the Calcutta Session of the Indian National Congress. Its first stanza was adopted by the Constituent Assembly of India as the national anthem on 24 January 1950.

title: Boniface I is elected pope in a contest with Eulalius
description: Boniface I became bishop of Rome in an election disputed by the supporters of Eulalius until Emperor Honorius settled the dispute. A contemporary of Augustine of Hippo, who dedicated works to him, he was active in maintaining church discipline.

skip: a single rail crash (the Ashtabula River railroad disaster): trivial for the site

title: The Treaty of St. Louis with the Council of Three Fires is proclaimed
description: The United States proclaimed the Treaty of St. Louis with the Council of Three Fires, the Ottawa, Ojibwe and Potawatomi of the Illinois and Milwaukee rivers. Ninian Edwards, William Clark and Auguste Chouteau had signed it at Portage des Sioux on 24 August.

title: Lakota warriors and the US Army fight at the Drexel Mission
description: A day after the Wounded Knee Massacre, in which 250 to 300 Lakota were killed, Lakota warriors and the United States Army fought on White Clay Creek north of Pine Ridge, South Dakota, where the Lakota were purported to have burned the Catholic Mission.

title: Vandals, Alans and Suebi cross the Rhine into Roman Gaul
description: Vandals, Alans and Suebi are traditionally held to have crossed the Rhine, one of the Late Roman Empire's most secure frontiers. The crossing began a wave of destruction of Roman cities and the collapse of Roman civic order in northern Gaul.

title: The Battle of Stones River begins near Murfreesboro, Tennessee
description: Bragg's Confederate Army of Tennessee and Rosecrans's Union Army of the Cumberland began a three-day battle near Murfreesboro, Tennessee, with the highest casualty rate of the war's major battles. It ended in a costly Union victory that lifted Northern morale.
